top_story: A fragile reopening after the Hormuz ceasefire unraveled on 26 June when a drone strike on a cargo ship in the strait prompted US attacks on Iranian military sites, resetting the crisis on a sharper military track. By 28 June, Iran had expanded the confrontation beyond the waterway with attacks on Bahrain and Kuwait and threats to halt talks entirely, while Trump’s threat to “annihilate” Iran signaled that coercion was displacing any remaining diplomatic restraint. The violence is also cutting into civilian life inside Iran, where strikes in Lamerd reportedly killed children at a sports hall, and into Gulf energy infrastructure, where a Saudi Aramco helicopter crash in Ras Tanura added to a climate of insecurity even without a clear link to the fighting. The regional picture is one of a maritime escalation spilling onto populated and economically vital terrain, raising the risk that deterrent signaling hardens into a broader conflict with direct human and commercial costs.
